claims.text: ALCE is an automatic benchmark for evaluating large language models' text generation with citations across three datasets: ASQA, QAMPARI, and ELI5.
On the ELI5 dataset, ChatGPT and GPT-4 baselines lack complete citation support approximately 50% of the time.
A closed-book LLM with post-hoc citation matching achieves competitive correctness but significantly lower citation recall compared to open-book retrieval models.
Summarizing retrieved passages into shorter summaries or snippets before prompting improves answer correctness across ALCE datasets.
Reranking multiple sampled generations based on automatic citation recall scores improves citation quality across ASQA and ELI5.
Increasing the number of in-context retrieved passages improves answer correctness and citation quality for GPT-4, but does not improve performance for ChatGPT.
Dense retrieval using GTR yields higher correctness and citation quality for LLM generation compared to DPR.
Instruction-tuned open-source models achieve higher correctness and citation quality compared to non-instruction-tuned base models.

evidence.description: We propose ALCE, the first benchmark for Automatic LLMs’ Citation Evaluation. ALCE collects a diverse set of questions and retrieval corpora... We compile three datasets that cover different types of questions and corpora— ASQA, QAMPARI, and ELI5.
For example, on the ELI5 dataset, around 50% generations of our ChatGPT and GPT-4 baselines are not fully supported by the cited passages.
CLOSED BOOK outperforms VANILLA in correctness on ELI5 and QAMPARI... However, citation recall of CLOSED BOOK+POST CITE is lower than VANILLA by 47% on ASQA.
We see a universal trend that SUMM or SNIPPET improves correctness, though on ASQA and ELI5, such an improvement comes at a cost of citation quality due to the lossy compression.
We observe that RERANK leads to consistent improvement in citation quality (on ASQA and ELI5)... On ASQA, citation recall improves from 73.6 to 84.8 for ChatGPT VANILLA.
GPT-4 (20-psg) achieves 44.4 EM Rec on ASQA compared to 41.3 for GPT-4 (5-psg), whereas including more passages with ChatGPT-16K does not improve results (36.1 EM Rec at 5-psg vs 36.1 at 20-psg).
Figure 4 (right) shows that GTR outperforms DPR in both correctness (40.4 vs 36.1 EM Rec) and citation quality (73.6 vs 65.0 citation recall) on ASQA.

Instruction-tuned models (Vicuna-13B and LLaMA-2-Chat) outperform the original LLaMA models in correctness (e.g. 31.9 EM Rec for Vicuna-13B vs 26.9 for LLaMA-13B) and considerably enhance citation quality (51.1 citation recall vs 10.6).

methodologies.name: ALCE Benchmark Framework
methodologies.description: An automated evaluation benchmark for evaluating end-to-end citation-augmented LLM outputs across fluency, factual correctness, and citation quality.

methodologies.name: NLI-based Citation Quality Evaluation
methodologies.description: Evaluates citation recall and precision by checking statement entailment against concatenated cited passages using the TRUE T5-11B NLI model.

limitations.text: Existing work mainly relies on commercial search engines and human evaluation, making it challenging to reproduce and compare different modeling approaches.
MAUVE metric is sensitive to output length and can provide unstable evaluation results.
Automatically generated claims for ELI5 correctness evaluation may not cover all possible answers due to the open-ended nature of the questions.
The NLI model used for citation precision evaluation cannot detect cases of partial support, leading to lower automated precision scores than human evaluation.
Curated benchmark datasets do not cover more challenging scenarios such as multi-hop reasoning, math reasoning, and code completion.

future_work.text: Developing better retrieval algorithms tailored for knowledge-intensive language tasks and LLM generation.
Advancing long-context LLMs capable of synthesizing information from multiple context documents without distraction.
Exploring direct supervised training and fine-tuning of LLMs to generate text with citations.
Training improved NLI models capable of recognizing partial citation support for more accurate automatic precision evaluation.
